utterances.text: If I suggested to you that from your window, you could see Simo Zaric, Miroslav Tadic and other soldiers standing at the corner of the street on the morning of the 17th of April, 17th of April, 1992, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I suggested to you that you saw such a sight and at the time that Mr. Tadic and Mr. Zaric were standing in uniform in the street, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I object to this line of questioning. I mean he already said that he haven't seen them. What's the difference whether according to what Mr. Di Fazio said, whether they were in uniforms or not. If he hadn't seen them, he hadn't seen them. MR. DI FAZIO: Fair enough. I'll withdraw my question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You provided a statement, didn't you, to officers of the OTP on the 26th of November, 1998, did you not? Those officers being two men named Yves Roy and Gary Selsky?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have an objection. The Prosecutor wishes to use the statement given by this witness on the 28th of November, 1998. We got this statement only today. We had never seen it before. If we had had this statement before, then we would have been able to use the circumstances stated here, both in the examination of the Prosecutors and our own witnesses. All the witnesses that we had and Blagoje Simic's witnesses have already passed. This manner of proceeding could incur great damage to both our defences and we are strongly objecting to the use of anything in this statement in the examination of this witness. MR. DI FAZIO: The statement doesn't concern the activities of Blagoje Simic at all. He's not mentioned. I'm sorry, I am sorry, my apologies, it does but nonetheless --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I thought, Mr. Di Fazio this is a statement which you said was already disclosed to the Defence. MR. DI FAZIO: It was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So there is no basis for this. MR. DI FAZIO: That was going to be my ultimate point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There is no basis for this objection. The Prosecution can go ahead. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you provide --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise but this statement was never disclosed to me. I am speaking for the Defence of Blagoje Simic. Today is the first time I see this statement. MR. DI FAZIO: I can't explain that. I don't know why Mr. Vukovic sees the statement for the first time. It was disclosed to the Defence in November of 1999. Perhaps there is a lack of communication, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because when we talk of the Defence we are including the whole Defence team. MR. DI FAZIO: Different lawyers at different times for different defendants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may assist the Chamber, I really have to say at my own risk that I see this document today for the first time and the case manager from the OTP told me that the Defence of Miroslav Tadic received this document on the 23rd of November, 1999. I will check that because I have all the receipts for all the documents disclosed to us in my office, but my client tells me that he had never seen this document before. And the Prosecution never gave us any proof of having served us the B/C/S version. What I know is when I asked the Prosecutor and when the case manager told us that this was disclosed to us on the 23rd of November, 1999, Blagoje Simic, that much I can say, had not surrendered at that time and he is certainly not aware of this statement so we want this to be on record if there is any intention to use the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you allow me, I just want to make a few remarks that I believe may assist the Trial Chamber. How did it come about that these statements were taken? The Defence of Simo Zaric provided certain statements to the investigators of the Tribunal and they presented us with a request, asking to talk to certain witnesses whose statements we had provided. Mr. Zaric was at the time in detention here and in consultation with him I gave our approval to the investigators for conducting an interview with nine witnesses that we had suggested and whose statements we had served. It was then noted that I as defender of Mr. Zaric would attend the interviews. However, investigator Yves Roy came with Mrs. Paterson, who wasn't present there but they were in touch with her by telephone, and they assumed the position that the counsel may not be present during the interviews. I did not want to insist, and we enabled them to talk to these witnesses. At that time, the witnesses concerned were designated as witnesses for the Defence of Simo Zaric. It is purely out of the wish to be cooperative towards the OTP that we had provided these statements. I never insisted that these statements be provided to us before, but if we -- if I hadn't insisted ultimately we would have never received them in the first place, and we never got the B/C/S translation, and now this problem is occurring in the Office of the Prosecutor because they discovered that only yesterday. This is the history of these statements. As far as I know, these statements were never given or read out to the witnesses in question in B/C/S so that they could know what they were signing and what was on record. So much for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, regardless of how it came about that these statements were taken, the Defence of Blagoje Simic objects to the part of the statement referring to Blagoje Simic being used now, because in year 2000, when this statement was disclosed, Blagoje Simic was not part of this case, and today is indeed the first time we see this statement. It could really incur great damage on the Defence of Blagoje Simic. That is the basis for our objection. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, the sole purpose that the Prosecution wants to make of this document is to impeach the credibility of this witness. That's its purpose. It's not going to be used against Blagoje Simic, for a start. Secondly, the -- if I may just move over to the screen, to my -- to the discovery log, our records show that on the 23rd, bracket 29th question mark closed bracket of November of 1999, witness statements of Defence witnesses taken by OTP were disclosed and this -- this statement of this witness is included in a number -- two Arnautovics and including a copy of a speech given by Mr. Zaric in that particular bundle of documents, a number of other witness statements. So our records indicate that the statement's been disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But not to the team of Mr. Blagoje Simic? MR. DI FAZIO: No. It would -- there is a name Simic there but I assume at that stage, it was Milan Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes because that was the Simic that was there. MR. DI FAZIO: But as I said we are not using the statement to -- against Blagoje Simic in any way. It's purely and simply to impeach the credibility of this witness. That's the purpose of it, inconsistent statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber is of the view that the Prosecution will be allowed to use the statement for impeachment purposes only. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now on the 26th of November, 1998, you gave a statement to officers from the OTP, Yves Roy and Gary Selsky did you not? I'm sorry, I haven't heard your answer.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that statement was reduced to English and was orally translated back to you by an interpreter, Irena Martinovic, correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you signed the bottom of each page of that statement, did you not?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I did sign, but I didn't know what the interpreter was saying to those who were writing things down into documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So you signed --

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: But I signed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You signed that statement. And at the end of the statement you signed a witness acknowledgement saying that the statement had been read over to you in the Croatian language and that it was true to the best of your knowledge and recollection and that you had given the statement voluntarily and that you were aware that it may be used in legal proceedings before the ICTY, correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I however disagree with one thing. I did not say how many soldiers there were in the 4th Detachment. I didn't know that then. Nor do I know it today. How many soldiers there were. Nor is it in my interest to know that. And they mentioned 1.800 to 2.000 troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you and when you gave the statement to the officers of the OTP, you were endeavouring to tell the truth and sought to tell the truth to those officers?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the statement, you said, did you not, "I live in a big house on main street and I saw from my window Simo Zaric, Miroslav Tadic and some other soldiers standing at the corner of the street in the morning on the 17th of April, 1992. Miro Tadic and Simo were standing in uniform in the street. I could see a lot of soldiers going back and forth near my corner, there was a tank, they were heavily armed and I don't know why they need all that army because there was no resistance in Samac." You said those things in your statement in November of 1998, did you not?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did state that. However, I did not see Simo Zaric and Miroslav Tadic. I heard their voices. There must have been a mistake by the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told the Trial Chamber this morning that Zaric and Tadic weren't present. Either on the 17th or the 18th. You've not described their presence at any time on the 17th or 18th in the vicinity of your house or the Dagovic house. Yet in your statement, you've said that they are on the corner, you've described them being in uniform, the presence of a tank. Which of those two versions should the Trial Chamber accept?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, to tell you honestly, I did not see them. I heard -- I don't know whether they were wearing a uniform. I don't know -- I know that Tadic never wore a uniform. He was always in civilian clothes. Simo Zaric was in the 4th Detachment and I believe he wore a uniform, military uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but let's take it point by point. First of all, you say this morning, and moments ago, that you didn't actually see them. You only heard them. In your statement, however, you say "I saw from my window Simo Zaric, Miroslav Tadic and some other soldiers." Now, what's the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just wait. What's the Trial Chamber to believe, that you only heard them or, as you said in your statement in 1998, that you saw them? Which one? Which version is correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: The correct version is what I have said. I didn't see them but I did hear their voices. They were standing around the corner behind a house, which was not very far from where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they doing there?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: They were standing at the corner, at the crossing. Simo Zaric knew many citizens of Samac because he had been there for a long time. He wouldn't allow the paramilitary formations to tour the houses, and he was standing at the door of a house where a lady and a girl resided and they told her, "Grandma, you should not be going out because there is a lot of shooting going on." And they didn't allow the paramilitary formations to enter other houses as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he wearing when you heard him?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, look, you've just told the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This was not fair, just for the record. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told the Trial Chamber moments ago, moments ago, that you only heard their voices, yet you described Mr. Zaric -- you described Mr. Zaric standing at the corner, at the crossing and Tadic. So you're just changing your evidence as questions are being asked, aren't you? Am I correct? Or am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I still stand by what I stated. I did not see them. I heard. Therefore, Tadic never wore a military uniform. Simo Zaric did. But I didn't see that. I do presume that he was wearing a military uniform at the time as well, since he was a member of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this morning you've described --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Arnautovic, I must warn that you've taken a solemn declaration to tell this Trial Chamber the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The truth, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, if you give false testimony, you can be prosecuted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move to another topic. That's the question of the vehicle that was there. Your evidence this morning has been that it was some sort of military vehicle. Having read the portions of your statement you made in 1998, to the effect that there was a tank, has that refreshed your memory and do you now agree that there was a tank in the vicinity of your home and the Dagovic home?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was a military vehicle. To tell you honestly, there was a difference between a tank and this military vehicle. This was of course a military vehicle, just as a tank is a military vehicle. You wouldn't see a civilian driving one. This vehicle, well, it's difficult for me to understand what it is. It had a light weaponry, it was moving. It was constantly in movement. And next to Dagovic's house, it just went by, and proceeded on to the villages that are there beyond.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement, you described it as a tank. Is there any reason for you not to have accurately described it, the vehicle, in your statement as a tank, back in 1998?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: This vehicle resembles a tank. It also has -- it has also caterpillars but it has a light weaponry, it is anti-aircraft machine-gun, it was some sort of a self-propelled vehicle. I'm not very familiar with weapons and such.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the Chamber can be certain that this vehicle, whatever it was, was on caterpillar tracks as tanks -- similar to what tanks use?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct? And it was a -- obviously a military vehicle and heavily armoured?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was a large vehicle, similar to the proportions of a tank?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It had a large weapon top of it, it must have been a large weapon if it's an anti-aircraft machine-gun, that's not a light machine-gun, that's a heavy machine-gun, correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely so, heavy machine-gun that can be used against aircrafts, but also infantry. It was maybe 20, 22 millimetre machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But for the purposes of the Trial Chamber, it was a larger, more powerful machine-gun than typically held or carried by soldiers?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, soldiers also have larger calibre 100, 120 millimetre. Well, this was a smaller calibre. It wasn't a gun, a cannon, but maybe heavy machine-gun, some 20, 22 millimetres, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you will agree with me that given all of these features that you've just described of this vehicle, and given the fact that in your statement of 1998 you yourself describe the vehicle as a tank, that a person seeing this tank on the 17th -- sorry, this vehicle on the 17th or 18th might easily have been mistaken as to the nature of this vehicle and describe it as a tank?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That's speculation whether a -- some other person could drive some conclusions. This is not a proper question in our opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. That's describing what another person, the mistake another person would mistake. MR. DI FAZIO: Perhaps it's a matter for submission, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the members of the 4th Detachment who were in your street went to the Dagovic house and sought weaponry but they did not come to your house, did they?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say that's because Fadil Topcagic directed them away from your house? In other words said that there is just old pensioners in the house and they need not search the premises?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Because he knew that there was -- there were no weapons in my house for sure, and there wasn't any -- anything really expensive for them to take away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So in your street, at least, the 4th Detachment was being selective as to which houses it searched, sorry, as to which premises it went to collect weapons?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could the counsel be more precise in this, using of word selective? MR. DI FAZIO: I think that's quite precise enough, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The question is quite clear. There is nothing wrong with it. The Prosecution can proceed. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was, in your street at least, the 4th Detachment was being selective as to which houses it went to collect weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, by and large, they knew who possessed weapons and they entered those dwellings or houses where they knew there were persons who possessed weapons, and they did not come to my house because I didn't have any. They went to Sabrija Dagovic's house and they found some weapons there. I -- now, as for the rest of my street which is actually one of the main streets, where there is most traffic, whether they went on, whether they proceeded, well probably they did, but there were no weapons because whoever had weapons either ran away, hid them or disposed of the weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you would agree with me, wouldn't you, that the sight of this large military vehicle and armed men was intimidating and frightening for you and the other citizens in the street?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I was not afraid because I wasn't guilty of anything, and when the vehicle was turning around, you know with the -- in the caterpillar tracks it usually turns around very slowly and the machine-gun was turned toward our house but this was merely because the vehicle was turning around and it proceeded on its way and actually went away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was the first time that you had seen tanks or sorry, a military vehicle similar to a tank, or whatever it might have been, in your street?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge or awareness as to why it was necessary for the 4th Detachment to collect weapons with the use of a large military vehicle?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, to put it frankly, they were expecting some sort of a resistance, because of the situation in the other part of the country, well, in the Republic of Croatia. There is only the Sava River dividing Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, and they were afraid of a possible attack from Croatia against Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The truth of the matter is, isn't it, that the tank, sorry, the large military vehicle, was used to intimidate the citizens of Bosanski Samac, frighten them and scare them into handing over their weapons?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I object. I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: How could this witness possibly know what the military personnel wanted to achieve with this military vehicle? He already answered that -- and I may be it was my mistake not to object the first time when he was asked what was the topic, why did they use this large military vehicle, the 4th Detachment, this witness was never a member of the 4th Detachment, but now I'm standing to this objection. This is a pure call for speculation. MR. DI FAZIO: All right. Perhaps if I rephrased the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the reason why the tank was used for the collection of weapons from houses? What was its role? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: The tank -- well, let's call it a tank but it was a self-propelled vehicle with caterpillar tracks, it did not intimidate people. The people were in their houses. It went in the direction of the Sava and Bosna Rivers because there you had machine-gun fire opened in the direction of Croatia and in the village Prud, where you had paramilitary formations, Croats gathering there, and this tank perhaps fired some ten, 20 rounds, any then withdrew and proceeded its way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that the vehicle, this military vehicle, actually discharged -- fired close to your house?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I object. This is exactly the opposite of what the witness said. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The translation seems to say that. MR. DI FAZIO: There was some sort of firing of the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: This tank perhaps fired some 10, 20 rounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes but not, he didn't say it was in front of his street. He said on -- MR. DI FAZIO: I asked the vicinity. In the vicinity. That's what I'm trying to find out from the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You can ask again, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, you said that the tank went off in the direction of the Sava and Bosna and then opened fire in the direction of Croatia. How far from your house and the Dagovic house was it when it fired?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: It was some 150, 200 metres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you could hear that clearly, the firing?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find that frightening and intimidating, that large --

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know it was firing in the direction of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Because I could hear and see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were actually out in the street looking at the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I saw it when it was returning and when it was going towards the Sava and Bosna Rivers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see it -- when it discharged, when it fired, was that in the presence of other houses, or sorry, were other houses nearby?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: It was in between the houses, because Samac is a very densely populated town. It would go between houses, and then discharge, and then withdraw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. One thing is absolutely crystal clear, though. You did hear that military vehicle fire and discharge?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it did so at a time when it was close to or nearby to residential homes in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But outside the town, toward, in the direction of the Sava River, down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. Re-examined by Mr. Pisarevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The vehicle that you saw in the street, in Pere Bosica Street, as you stated, had a machine-gun on top. In order to clarify what you saw, first we will say that you said that it was a self-propelled armoured vehicle with this machine-gun, correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this vehicle, just as tanks do, have a tank barrel, which is something that actually distinguishes a tank from other armoured vehicle?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, it did not have a barrel. I know what a gun is. This was a heavy machine-gun, let's call it that way, an anti-aircraft weapon and maybe also anti-infantry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is not what we are talking about. Let's just make a distinction. On a tank, you have the long barrel and on this particular vehicle that you saw on the 18th of April, 1992, there was no such tank barrel?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Correct. There wasn't any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were answering the Prosecutor's question a moment ago, you said that you heard some shooting, that some sort of a combat vehicle was opening fire. When you heard the fire open, was it on the 18th of April or were you actually talking about something that happened in the aftermath of the 18th of April?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot give you a precise date but perhaps it was on the 20th or the 25th or maybe even later, that on that day, however, there wasn't such fire. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, the witness clearly described the episode happening very shortly after the episode that he witnessed at the Dagovic house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: He said it turned around and went off down the road and then he heard the sound of fire so we know clearly that the witness has linked it to that episode and I think in his evidence he said that this happened on the 18th. It's not a matter that I opened up in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If the witness decides to change his evidence now and then, that's up to Mr. Pisarevic and up to the witness as to what he can remember and what type of picture he wants to present. He has already been warned about telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour. However, there is another problem. The Prosecution does not understand the town of Samac. I shall remind you that the witness said that this armoured combat vehicle went towards Tisina, towards the villages and when he was explaining --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, the evidence given by this witness is on record, just go ahead with your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This vehicle that you saw that passed by and you said that it went to Tisina, did that vehicle shoot from that machine-gun at that moment at that time? Did you see that or did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: That day, I did not hear it. However, this vehicle was coming from the opposite street. It went, it did not stop, it turned around, and it went down there towards the villages, the village is called Tisina. But there was shooting on that day too, now whether that vehicle was there or not, perhaps it was another vehicle or another machine-gun or another cannon or whatever. I don't know. I didn't see this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, the question for you is did you see that vehicle, which passed in front of your window, in front of your house, and which went towards Tisina, that is on the opposite side of the village of Prud and the village of -- and the Republic of Croatia, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that vehicle shoot on that day after it passed by?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I did not hear any shooting that day, but there was shooting coming from all sorts of things, machine-guns, whatever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just interested in that vehicle now. On that day, the 17th and 18th, did you leave your house and go out into the street?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you said to the Prosecutor that you heard the voice of Simo Zaric and Miroslav Tadic, did that voice come from the street of Pere Bosica or did it come from another street, this voice that you heard?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Another street, opposite.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that street intersect with --

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: The street of Pere Bosica, it does, it does intersect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the name of this street?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Now it's called Cara Dusana.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that before it was called the street Edvarda Kardelja?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Edvarda Kardelja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall, when you gave a statement to the representatives of the OTP in Samac in 1998, whether the interpreter, Martinovic, read this statement out to you in the Serbian, Croatian or Bosnian language?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, she didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This statement, was it ever put to you in the Serbian language? Did you ever read it in the Serbian language and then sign it?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means that you signed only the English version. Since not everything is recorded in the transcript, all right, so you just signed the English version?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I made the statement and I signed it immediately. Nothing else. It was not read out to me, I didn't get anything afterwards, nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know English?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, no further questions. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I just have one question, Mr. Arnautovic. I just want to know how far from your house is the intersection of the two streets mentioned, Pere Bosica and Edvarda Kardelja streets? So this intersection where you say you heard Mr. Zaric's voice coming from, how far is it away, approximately, from your house and where you were in that house perhaps?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Exactly nine metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Mr. Arnautovic, when you told us about certain and different observations you made on that very day, I got the impression, perhaps I misunderstood what you said, but I got the impression that you made your observations through your window in your apartment. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I did see but I did not see that street. I saw the intersection, but I did not see anybody behind the street but I heard and recognised Simo Zaric's voice and Miroslav Tadic's.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Through the window?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: They were talking. Oh, no, not through the window. I was in the yard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: So you went out of your house?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I was not in the house itself but it was -- I was in my yard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: In the front of your house or at the back?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Behind the house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Okay. But the military vehicle you were talking about, it was moving along the Pere Bosica Street, if I understood you correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: But you could see it even if you -- when you were in the yard behind your house?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I could see it, but at that moment, when the vehicle was passing by, I was in the house with my wife.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: And watched it through your window?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that that military vehicle was moving on caterpillar tracks and that it had a machine-gun of whatever calibre, it's not so interesting but what I'm interested in, did it have only one barrel?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Only one barrel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Then you said, if I understood you correctly, first when you observed that vehicle, it was moving in the direction from east to west. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: This vehicle was moving from the north to the east.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: But your street, Pere Bosica, is, according to the map I have in front of me, almost running in the direction west-east. So to say from the direction of the Bosna River --

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: -- towards the villages.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: And from which direction --

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Yes, okay. From which direction did the vehicle arrive when you first observed it? From the east or from the west?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: From the north. From the Sava River.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: But that couldn't be along the Pere Bosica street. It must have been along another street.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No. No. This vehicle came from the street of Cara Dusana, and it turned into the street of Pere Bosica, and then it proceeded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: In which direction, east or west?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: East.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: But you said it turned around.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it came from the north, and then it turned to the east, because my house is at the intersection of Pere Bosica and Edvarda Kardelja. Only nine metres away, so I could see all of this from the window, where it was going and where it came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Okay. And then we -- when it had passed by, it went in the direction, east direction, am I right?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Then you told us that after some 100 metres, you could either watch or in some way recognise that it fired some 20 rounds?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I did not see that and I did not hear that. This vehicle went on. It went to the villages down there, perhaps two or three kilometres away from Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: So when we were talking about a military vehicle firing some 20 rounds, you are talking about another occasion?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Now, whether that vehicle fired then, on the other side, because Samac is about two or three kilometres long, now, whether it fired down there, towards Croatia or not, is something that I don't know. Only shooting was heard. There was quite a bit of shooting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: So you couldn't exactly define whether it was that vehicle or some other --

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Couldn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you very much for giving evidence. You are now finished. You may leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Examined by Mr. Lazarevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the proofing yesterday, I told you that for the purposes of the transcript, it would be best for you to wait for me to finish my question and then you count to 2 and then you answer the question so that everything would be recorded in the transcript the way you put it and the way it is expected to be. Could you now please, for the purposes of the record, give us your full name and surname?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Mustafa Omeranovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please give me the date of your birth.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: The 8th of July, 1940.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, where were you born?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: In Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where you live now?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Also in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, what is your profession?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm a retired person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, before you retired, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: I was an administrative clerk at the Mebos company in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, did you do your military service in the Yugoslav People's Army? If so, tell us when and where.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: I served in Croatia in Bjelovar in 1964. I beg your pardon, in 1964, or rather from 1964, until 1966.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have any rank in the military?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please give us your ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: A Muslim, a Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, have you ever been a member of any political party, and are you now a member of any political party?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: No, never. I've never been a member of any party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you perhaps in the League of Communists?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: No in my family, it was only one son, nobody else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, are you married?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any children?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I have three children, two sons and one daughter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to have a complete picture, could you please tell us what is your wife's name?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Koviljka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your wife related to Mr. Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, she is his sister.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, now I would like to move on very briefly, there is no need to dwell on this very long. These are matters that had been explained here many times. Were you a member of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, in which way did you become a member of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you know what the situation was like. It suited me best that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive mobilisation call-up papers?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean during the war?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, when did you become a member of the detachment?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that was sometime in January, 1992, or was it spring or -- no, January.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, these are things that are well known here already but just tell us who the commander and deputy commander of the 4th Detachment were?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: The first commander was Radovan Antic and he was replaced by Savic, and then there was a change and then --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much I mean we are not all that interested in that part. I'm more interested in the following. Can you tell us what Mr. Zaric was in the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was just in the staff of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, what were you in the 4th Detachment? Did you have any particular duty there?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I commanded a platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to clarify this for the Trial Chamber, what does a platoon mean? How many people does it involve approximately?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: About ten people, ten, 12. A platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. Tell me, did you get any weapons from the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you first tell me what you got, what kind of weapon, when you became a member of the detachment?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I got a Russian automatic rifle, an old one, from the Second World War.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just tell me where did you get this weapon actually?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: We all got it near Brcko. I can't remember now -- I beg your pardon. We got it near Brcko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this perhaps at a military exercise?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Like familiarisation with weapons and...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us where is your house in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Vuka Karadzica, number 27.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's close to the centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it perhaps near the market?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, about 50 metres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me now, in order to have a complete picture, this is a joint yard where there are two houses actually?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me now, in addition to your house, whose is the other house in that yard?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: It's my mother's house.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreter did not hear the rest of the answer, whose house it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, the interpreters are telling us that they could not hear you, that they could not fully hear your answer. So you said that it was your mother's house, and tell me what did you say about the second house, the other house?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: My mother's house faces the street and my house is behind it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me now, in any period, was your house or your mother's house used for storing weapons?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: No way. Why would any such thing be done? There was no need to do that. We were all armed. I said that. We received weapons near Brcko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me now, your neighbours on the left-hand side, on the right-hand side, across the street, and generally speaking down the street, along the street, what was the average ethnic background of your neighbours?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll tell you straight away, there were two Serb marriages and there was a purely Croat marriage, and all the rest were Muslims, Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, does your street have a street lighting during the night?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Always. Even during the night -- during the war, during the night, if there was electricity, there were always street lights on. This was one of the best-lit streets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Among your neighbours and you said that they were predominantly Bosniak --

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any members of the Party of Democratic Action?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think that 90 per cent were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So I'm just going to put one more question to you in relation to this, although you've practically answered it already. At any given point in time, did you, together with Mr. Simo Zaric, in that street, in front of your house, or rather in front of your mother's house, did you unload boxes of military weapons from a truck and carry it into your backyard?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you, sir. I have already said what the ethnic composition was in my street. Had I taken a bottle of whiskey and carried it through the street and carried it into the home, into my home, everybody would have seen it, everybody, even if I were carrying it in a shopping bag but two trucks, two trucks, that is so absurd. First of all I would not allow any such thing to happen in front of my house, and it didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just ask you for a brief answer, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's time for our usual break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We will take our break and continue at 1250 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before Mr. Lazarevic continues, Prosecution just places on the record an objection to the evidence just having been led on the basis that it is contrary to the provisions of Rule 90(H) (ii) in relation to the cross-examination of Mr. Nusret Hadzijusufovic at pages T 6995 to 6996. A contrary case of the Defence was not put to Mr. Hadzijusufovic when he was cross-examined on that occasion so it infringes the rule and the Prosecution formally notes its objection to that evidence being led.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is just for the record, then I may need not give any answer to this but if I remember correctly and I also checked through the transcript, Mr. Hadzijusufovic was cross-examined in respect to this fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's not what I'm saying. I'm saying he was certainly cross-examined but Rule 90(H)(ii) requires the cross-examining party to put a contrary case, the words are shall put to the witness the nature of the case of the party for whom that counsel appears which is in contradiction of the evidence given by the witness. The cross-examination doesn't suggest a case which is contrary it in fact suggests something which could come close, something which is more mistaken rather than contrary. If Your Honours look at T 6995 to T 6996 and of course the difficulty with my raising it at this point is the Prosecution is of course not on notice from the four lines provided in the Rule 71 summary, in inverted commas, that the witness is a Muslim from Bosanski Samac, he will testify on isolated incidents involving Mr. Zaric, such as incarceration at the SUP building of the witness and other members of the 4th Detachment and the release, involvement of Mr. Zaric in their release. Witness Ibrahim Salkic mentioned all these incidents in his testimony, 40 minutes, we received some -- I received this morning a proofing note alluding to this particular incident. As a result of that I went to the transcript. Until I received this on my desk at 9.00 this morning, the Prosecution had no -- I had no notice that evidence was going to be led on this particular point from this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic, I think the Trial Chamber has mentioned this before in relation to other witnesses, that you're going outside the summary that was provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, if I may just say one thing, these witnesses arrived here in The Hague yesterday. It was the first time that I saw them was at 6.00 a.m. and I informed my colleague, Mr. Weiner about the content of what -- about some information that I received from the witness. I really had no much time to inform everybody because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's not the point. You are the Defence counsel. You prepare the summaries. You are the person who decides which witness will discuss what type of evidence. And that's what you did. And you prepared a summary and provided the Chamber and the Prosecution, and you stick to that. There is no formal application to add anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour is right and I will go right to the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So that the Prosecution's objection is actually correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I was just going to confirm what attorney Lazarevic said. He did provide full summary to us last evening which was just upon completion of his proofing. I had called him about dinner time and he said I was going to start proofing, and to call back around 10.00 last night and we did -- he did provide, as a gentleman and according to his writ, full summary as to what his witness was going to be testifying about, and with regard to those different facts. So I am confirming what Mr. Lazarevic has said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but the point is there is no application to the Trial Chamber to add any other matters to the summary that was filed. Counsel is supposed to stick to the summaries that were filed, as matters which their witnesses were going to discuss. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, let us move now to the night between the 16th and the 17th of April, 1992. Tell me kindly, where were you in the evening hours of the 17th -- 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: I was at home. Since my mother is old and sickly, I was together with her in the same room there was me, my wife and my mother. We were alone that night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says here that you were all three of you in one room?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct. Since she is sickly, she needed help.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, did anything happen during the night?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were awakened, my wife and I, around 3.00 a.m. by a detonation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get out of your home? Did you do anything about it?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I stayed inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 17th of April, 1992, around noon, what was going on?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: That is right. Around noon, on the 17th of April, two members of paramilitary units came accompanied by one police officer wearing a beret, and there was also a police vehicle. They asked me to turn over the weapon that I had. I did so, and then they picked me up, put me in their car and drove me to the SUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you show them the weapon that you received as a member of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you show them perhaps the licence as well for that weapon?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but they wouldn't hear anything. They just made me get into the car, they took my weapon and drove me to the SUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived to the SUP building, what happened next? When you got out of the car outside the SUP?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: They opened the boot of the car but I didn't have time to pick up the weapon that I was supposed to carry into the SUP building myself, because a man in a camouflage uniform came up to me and started to beat me. As a result of that -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you all right? Sir? Do you want a small break, perhaps ten minutes?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. Please. Just let me overcome this small crisis. It always gets over me when I talk about it. I received a bad beating. I can show the consequences to the Chamber. My teeth, for instance. After that, they took me inside and put me in a room where some detainees were already locked up, some people from the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, are you able to continue?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I am. I'm sorry for this little disturbance. I always get a little emotional when I remember it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go on, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Just to the witness, if you're not feeling well and you need to have a break, you should inform us. We can have a break to allow you to recover.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's all right. I'm fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you told us that you were badly beaten before coming into the SUP building, and that you were locked up in a room where there were more members of the 4th Detachment. Tell me, please, if you can remember, who were those other members of the 4th Detachment that you found imprisoned there?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Just give me a minute. Muharem Kapetanovic, Hajrudin Seljakovic, Hasim Avdic, and Tadija whose surname I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it Brandic perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This room where you were locked up, can you remember that room and describe it?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: There were two box cells where other people were detained, whereas we were in a small hallway, because we simply couldn't fit in there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean that room had two little box cells with bars?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Right, right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, how long did you remain in detention in the SUP building?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: I spent the night there and was released in the morning. In fact, not in the morning but in the afternoon of the next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did it come about that you were able to get out of that cell?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't rightly know. Zaric showed up, and this other man Nikolic, and they said that members of the 4th Detachment should come out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a policeman accompanying Zaric?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: A policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me now, were you the only one who got out of the SUP building at that time or were the others able to get out too?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: The others --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just take it easy. Please answer slowly and wait for my question to finish. I can see that you are a little upset. So those others that you enumerated, were they also released at the same time as you were?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were released, did Mr. Zaric tell you how it came about that you were released? Because you are his brother-in-law; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they said that members of the 4th Detachment should get out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Zaric ever tell you the story of how it came about in the first place that you were able to get out?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that it was through the intervention of Colonel - what's his name - Nikolic. A military man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were told by Zaric that this was so, right?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were released, did you go back to the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no way. I was no longer a member of the 4th Detachment. I was disarmed and I was not their member any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you were disarmed, you mean that those two men in the camouflage uniform and this policeman took the weapon away from you?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, what did you do afterwards?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: The next day, I went to buy cigarettes, and on my way, I ran into a friend who offered me a job of some sort, and the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you accept it?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, until when did you continue to work at the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid I may be mistaken about the date of that next day. I was talking about. I worked until end February, early March, when the work obligation was abolished. In that period from the 1st of January, 1993, until the 31st of July, I worked in the company where I had been employed before, and that was my work obligation, and after that period, I was again sent back to the Red Cross, which again was a work obligation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me the name of the company where you worked?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Mebos is the name of the company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't tell me or perhaps -- that time that you spent working at the Red Cross, what year was that?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: 1992. I said until January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all we wanted to hear. You first worked at the Red Cross, then you return to Mebos and then you went to work again in the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this second spell at the Red Cross, when did it end?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: The end of February, when the law of Republika Srpska on the abolishment of the work obligation was adopted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which year was that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Does any other counsel wish to examine this witness? No? The Prosecution? Cross-examined by Mr. Re:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Omeranovic. David Re is my name, from the Prosecution. I'm going to ask you some questions about your testimony and what happened. You understand my role?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I just ask you if you could possibly listen very carefully to the question I ask and answer the question that I ask you and if anything upsets you, please don't hesitate to stop or ask for a pause, but I will try not in any way to upset you by reliving any of those things. Do you understand that, sir? Could you answer that? I saw you nod. I think you said yes.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When -- in your evidence you said that you had been issued with a -- I think an old Russian weapon. Was that a Kalashnikov?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: No. It was a weapon called spagin an old weapon from the Second World War.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For those of us who aren't aware, is it similar in any way to a Kalashnikov?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Not at all. It is a weapon that uses pistol ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your house, Mr. Omeranovic, is about 50 metres or so from the marketplace in Bosanski Samac, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And trucks frequently park in the vicinity of your house, delivering their produce to markets, don't they?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, the market is 50 metres away from me. In my street, it was forbidden to park vehicles, regardless of whether they were passenger or freight vehicles. You were allowed to stop but not to park, and parking is defined as stopping for more than 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you and for the Trial Chamber's benefit I asked that question in relation to the cross-examination of Mr. Nusret Hadzijusufovic, at transcript page 6996 in which this was actually suggested to Mr. Nusret Hadzijusufovic. Hence my comment earlier about Rule 90(H)(ii). Now, sir, when you were arrested by paramilitaries, you said it was on the -- I think your evidence here was that it was on the 17th of April, 1992. That's the morning of the takeover, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The -- your arrest, you were given no reason for your arrest, were you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you were taken to the SUP, and imprisoned there, the only other people there were Muslims and Croats, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago, I just want to clarify something you said. You were given no reason for your arrest, you said no, yes. It's a little bit unclear. Were you given a reason for your arrest?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: No. They didn't say anything. They didn't give me a reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the period you were detained, no Muslims or Croats were able to -- I withdraw that. Mr. Zaric came to the police station and came to the door of the area where you were imprisoned and said, "I want my guys out of here" or something to that effect, didn't he? Meaning members of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the period you were imprisoned, that day or night or so, no Muslims or Croats --

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the period of your imprisonment or detention at the SUP, no Muslims or Croats did what Mr. Zaric did, that is came to the building or came to the door of the area where you were imprisoned and said, "Look, I want the Muslims out or I want the Croats out," did they?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand. We were all Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... particularly clear for the witness. I had to read it twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll rephrase it if it's not clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Omeranovic, Mr. Zaric, a Serb came to the door and you just agreed said, I want members of the 4th Detachment out, my guys. While you were there, no Muslims or Croats came to the door, like Mr. Zaric had done and said, look, I want the Muslims released or I want the Croats released. That didn't happen, did it?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I don't know whether anyone had come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just asking you whether you saw it in the time you were detained at the SUP, you saw any Muslims or Croats come to the door and say, "I want the Muslims out or I want the Croats out." It's only Mr. Zaric who was able to do that.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I have something in my pocket now. Can you see from where you're standing what it is? I don't think you can see. That's -- that's the same reason why I couldn't see if anyone had come to the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you hear anyone? All I'm asking you if anyone else while you were in prison there came asking for the release of anyone else. That's all I'm asking you. What you saw, what you heard.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Other Muslims were released too, but I don't know through whose intervention. All I know is that they were released.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who those Muslims are? Are you able to tell us now?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: But of course. One of them -- actually both of them are deceased. One of them lived in Denmark, and I can't remember if there were any others or who they were. They were released before me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The two who were released can you remember their names? That's all I want to know.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: But of course. Namik Bajzovik is the name of one of them. And the other's family name is Hadzialagic but no, I can't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they members of the 4th Detachment or the JNA, sir?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: No, they weren't. As far as I know, to tell you, I only knew those of my platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you're saying is you just don't know whether they were members of the JNA or the 4th Detachment because the only people you knew who were in the 4th Detachment were those in your platoon? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I knew also the -- these four men who were there. I also knew them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When these paramilitaries came and arrested you, it was the paramilitary with the SDS who came to your house and arrested you, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have an objection. The witness has already said that it was the paramilitary units and policemen who arrested him. Someone unknown to him, wearing a beret. And therefore he cannot know who -- and he said he didn't know who the man was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Surely the witness must be able to answer. I can refresh his memory from another document but I'm just asking him to establish something first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vukovic, the question put to the witness is one which the witness can answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question to you, Mr. Omeranovic, is when you were arrested, it was paramilitaries with the SDS who arrested you, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: No. They weren't members of the SDS. Well, actually, how could I have known whether they were members of the SDS? Those in the camouflage uniforms and the policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you made a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 27th of November, 1998, to Irena Martinovic as the interpreter and Mr. Yves Roy and Gary Selsky as the investigators in Bosanski Samac, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA OMERANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have an objection. It is the same thing that we had with the previous witness, Jusuf Arnautovic. It's the same question. It's the statement that was taken by the Prosecution in 1998 and I have never seen it. I haven't seen it to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I asked the witness if he made a statement. That was my question. And he's already agreed he made a statement. Now, the statement was of course disclosed to the Defence, particularly Mr. Zaric, in the same batch as the previous witness, on the same day. Because the OTP investigators were in Bosanski Samac that week. They took statements from the witnesses, including some who have given evidence today. These have been provided to the Defence years ago, and there was reciprocal disclosure was invoked and Mr. Zaric's Defence gave us a copy of Mr. Omeranovic's statement to Mr. Pisarevic. The statements have been swapped to so speak and my question was only, did you make a statement. The objection if any is premature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps we wait and see where the Prosecution is going.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Maybe I can assist my colleague, Mr. David. The truth is that we received this statement in 1999, a year after the statement was given to the Prosecution. It was on Status Conference, I remember it very well, because I was present at that point, that we raised that issue before the Pre-Trial Chamber because Ms. Nancy Paterson who was in charge of this case for the Prosecution at the moment why we haven't been provided with nine statements that our witnesses, witnesses from the list of Mr. Zaric's Defence, why we haven't been provided with these nine statements. And then the Trial Chamber issued an order to the Prosecution to disclose this to the Defence of Mr. Zaric, Tadic and Mr. Milan Simic, and this is something that I remember very clearly. So we haven't been given these statements in 1998 when they were made. It was at least one year later, maybe more than that. And by that time, at that Status Conference, I remember also that very well, Mr. Blagoje Simic was not here in the detention unit. He didn't surrender to the Tribunal, and this is what I remember very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you for the explanation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just agreed that you made this statement sir, and the statement was read to you by in -- was read to you by Irena Martinovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have made an objection and we are actually request that the statements made by this witness in this particular statement not be a matter of questioning because they might be prejudicial for our case. We haven't seen to this very day. This was the first time today that we've seen this statement taken by the Prosecution back in 1998. I haven't seen it at all. Not even during the break, and I still don't have it. This would be irrelevant because we have never seen it and we were unable to use the statements by his witness while we were questioning the Prosecution witnesses and the witnesses of the Defence for Mr. Blagoje Simic, and we explicitly object to the fact that the statements given by this witness in this particular statement be put to the witness today during this examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour the statement was disclosed to Mr. Pantelic who was then acting for Mr. Milan Simic. He has a copy of it if Mr. Vukovic doesn't. I can provide him with a copy of it now but it's in relation to this witness, not Dr. Simic. It's not him, it's impeachment possibly, I don't know I want to ask the witness whether he agrees with what he said earlier, four years ago. It's not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What Mr. Vukovic has said and which appears to be the position, Mr. -- Dr. Blagoje Simic hadn't yet been joined to this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: He may well not have but that's not what I'm using this statement for. I want to ask this witness about some statements he made in 1998 to OTP investigators which were provided to the lawyers who provided us with his own statement and ask him about that and the evidence he's given here, asking him if it's the same.
